issues.text: I cannot tell what it means for a reference to 'leave its method', and the sentence seems to bend the Core concepts rule that class objects live on the heap. The lesson tells me to keep the heap model, so the main idea survives, but I stopped and re-read here in the paragraph that carries the main difference.
issues.fix: Drop the condition 'when no reference to it ever leaves its method', or move the whole aside to the end of the paragraph so it does not interrupt the class/struct explanation.

issues.quote: because the runtime can keep memory it took back for its next objects.
issues.text: Section 4 says the garbage collector 'takes back' memory, so I pictured it leaving my process. Here memory that was taken back still counts for the process, which reads like the opposite. I get the gist (the number may not fall) but not why.
issues.fix: Either end the bullet at 'or not visibly at all.' or add a few words saying the memory is taken back from the dead object but kept by the process for its next objects.

issues.quote: You notice this when you watch your process's memory in a tool that shows each process's memory.

issues.quote: When `Run` returns, its frame goes at once, before its caller's, so this memory needs no decision to release, unlike the heap object below, which waits for the garbage collector.

issues.fix: Split after 'before its caller's.' and start a new sentence: 'Nobody has to decide to release this memory; the heap object below is different, it waits for the garbage collector.'
